title: Green Crackers for Diwali 2026: Types, Rules and How to Spot a Fake
excerpt: CSIR-NEERI green crackers cut particulate emissions by at least 30%, but only certified products with a verifiable QR code count — and Mumbai tests this season found banned barium in several products sold as green.
body:
• Green crackers are CSIR-NEERI formulations designed to cut particulate matter emissions by at least 30% against conventional crackers; they are not smoke-free.
  • The three types are SWAS (safe water releaser), STAR (safe thermite cracker) and SAFAL (safe minimal aluminium).
  • Rules are local: West Bengal, for example, allows only certified green crackers, on Diwali between 8 p.m. and 10 p.m., with sound caps of 125 dB for sound-emitting and 90 dB for light-emitting crackers.
  • Verify before you buy: a genuine pack carries the CSIR-NEERI logo and a QR code that checks out in the CSIR-NEERI app. Prices vary by product and city; no official price list exists.

Every Diwali, the same question returns with the smoke: are green crackers actually better, and what exactly is allowed? The short answer is that green crackers are a regulated category, not a marketing label — and this year, enforcement and a counterfeit problem are as much a part of the story as the chemistry.

What makes a cracker 'green'

Green crackers were developed under guidelines from the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research–National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI). Their modified chemical composition is designed to deliver at least a 30% reduction in particulate matter emissions, and approved formulations avoid prohibited chemicals such as barium nitrate. They still produce smoke and noise — the claim is lower emissions, not none.

The three CSIR formulations are SWAS, a safe water releaser that suppresses dust by releasing water vapour; STAR, a safe thermite cracker formulated without potassium nitrate and sulphur; and SAFAL, a safe minimal aluminium formulation that cuts the metal content of the flash powder. Between them they cover the standard Diwali range of flower pots, sparklers, rockets and sound crackers.

The rules this year

The Supreme Court's position in the long-running case is that it will neither impose a complete ban nor allow unrestricted use, so the operative rules are set state by state. In West Bengal, the government announced that only pollution-board-certified green crackers may be sold or burst this season: on Diwali the window is 8 p.m. to 10 p.m., and on Chhath Puja 6 a.m. to 8 a.m., with noise capped at 125 decibels for sound-emitting crackers and 90 decibels for light-emitting ones, according to The CSR Journal's report of the Nabanna briefing. Unauthorised sky lanterns are banned outright in the state. Other states and districts set their own windows — Kangra district, for instance, has permitted green crackers only between 8 p.m. and 10 p.m. on Diwali night — so the rule that matters is your local administration's, not a national one.

The fake problem

Certification is the weak point. In Mumbai, the Awaaz Foundation tested 17 firecracker varieties bought on Mohammed Ali Road and in Kurla on October 9 and 10 and reported barium — a substance the Supreme Court has prohibited in firecrackers — in several products sold as green or sustainable, with the highest concentration, 27.405%, in a product called Serpent Egg Big. Four of the 17 samples did not disclose their chemical composition, five had no QR code, and of the 12 with codes, four reportedly did not verify through the CSIR-NEERI app; eleven did not display permitted noise limits, according to the foundation's findings reported by Mumbai TV News. The foundation's founder, Sumaira Abdulali, wrote to Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis seeking stronger enforcement.

Buying without getting fooled

Two features authenticate a pack: the official CSIR-NEERI logo and a QR code. Scanning the code with the 'CSIR NEERI Green QR Code' app should return the manufacturer's details and confirm the product. If the code does not verify, treat the pack as conventional — whatever the box claims. Business Today's Diwali guide covers types and where-to-buy questions; prices vary by brand, product and city, and there is no official rate card, so a licensed seller and a verifiable code matter more than a quoted price.
